description: Behavioral exercises: the coach sets a concrete task and grades the SUBMITTED ARTIFACT (code), not a self-report. Objective `checks` (regex over the submission) give a keyless, deterministic signal; the code-reading rubric judge integrates them. Keyed by competency_id from competency_map.json.

exercises.title: Resilient batch of LLM calls
exercises.prompt: Write an async function `run_batch(prompts, call_llm)` that runs ~500 LLM calls concurrently but safely: cap concurrency, retry transient failures with backoff, apply a per-call timeout, and return results without letting one failure sink the batch.
exercises.rubric: L4 code: async with an explicit concurrency cap (Semaphore), retry with backoff, per-call timeout (wait_for), and it isolates per-call failures. L2: a plain loop or unbounded gather with no limits/retries/timeouts.

exercises.title: Schema-valid JSON with recovery
exercises.prompt: Write `get_person(text, call_llm)` that returns a validated object with fields name:str and age:int from the model. Use a schema, validate the output, and recover (retry) on invalid output instead of trusting raw text.
exercises.rubric: L4: typed schema (Pydantic/JSON schema / structured-output mode), explicit validation, and a retry that feeds the error back. L2: json.loads on free text with no validation or recovery.

exercises.title: Structure-aware chunker
exercises.prompt: Write `chunk_document(text)` for legal contracts. Don't just cut every N characters: respect structure (sections/paragraphs), use overlap, and attach metadata to each chunk.
exercises.rubric: L4: splits on structural boundaries, configurable overlap, per-chunk metadata, reasons about size. L2: fixed-size slicing with no overlap/structure.

checks.description: Splits on structure, not just fixed size

exercises.title: Bound a runaway agent loop
exercises.prompt: Here is an agent loop that can spin forever and blindly trusts tool calls. Rewrite `run_agent(task, tools)` to be reliable: cap the steps, validate tool selection/args, handle tool errors, and terminate cleanly.
exercises.rubric: L4: explicit step limit, validated tool dispatch, error handling/fallback, clear termination. L2: unbounded while loop, no validation or guards.

exercises.title: Harden a doc-reading tool
exercises.prompt: Write `handle_document(user_doc, run_tool)` where the document is UNTRUSTED and the agent can call tools. Defend against prompt injection: isolate untrusted content, restrict which tools/args are allowed, and never execute instructions from the document.
exercises.rubric: L4: treats content as data (delimiters/separate channel), tool allow-list with arg checks, no execution of doc-derived commands. L2: concatenates the doc into the prompt and trusts it.

exercises.title: Embed, index, and retrieve
exercises.prompt: Write `build_retriever(docs, embed_fn)` that embeds and indexes docs, plus `search(query, k)` returning the top-k by cosine similarity. Batch the embeddings, normalize the vectors, and keep the embedding model a swappable parameter (`embed_fn`) so it can be evaluated/changed — don't hard-code one.
exercises.rubric: L4: batched embedding, normalized vectors with cosine similarity, top-k selection, and a swappable embedding function (reasons about model choice). L2: embeds one-at-a-time, raw dot product on unnormalized vectors, a single hard-coded model.

exercises.title: Hybrid search with re-ranking
exercises.prompt: Implement `hybrid_search(query, docs, k)` that combines lexical retrieval (BM25/keyword) with dense (embedding) retrieval, fuses the two rankings (e.g. Reciprocal Rank Fusion or weighted scores), then re-ranks the top candidates before returning k results.
exercises.rubric: L4: both a lexical and a dense signal, an explicit fusion step (RRF/weighted), and a re-rank of the top candidates. L2: a single retrieval method with no fusion or re-rank.

exercises.title: Measure retrieval quality
exercises.prompt: Write `evaluate_retrieval(queries, retriever)` where each query carries its known relevant doc ids. Compute recall@k and precision@k (MRR too if you can) across the set and return the aggregate metrics — not a vibe check on a couple of examples.
exercises.rubric: L4: uses labeled relevant ids, computes recall@k and precision@k (and/or MRR), aggregates across all queries. L2: eyeballs a few results, no labels or metrics.

exercises.title: Robust tool dispatch
exercises.prompt: Write `dispatch(tool_call, tools)` where `tool_call` is a model-produced object like {"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}. Look the tool up in a registry, validate the arguments against its schema, call it, and return a structured result — handling unknown tools and bad arguments without crashing (and without eval/getattr on the name).
exercises.rubric: L4: registry lookup, argument validation against a schema, error handling for unknown tool / bad args, structured result. L2: getattr/eval on the tool name, no validation, unguarded call.

checks.description: Looks up tool in a registry
No eval/exec on the tool name

exercises.title: A bounded ReAct loop
exercises.prompt: Implement `react(task, tools, call_llm)` as a ReAct loop: the model alternates Thought → Action (a tool call) → Observation until it produces a Final Answer. Cap the number of iterations, feed each observation back into the context, and terminate cleanly on a final answer or when the cap is hit.
exercises.rubric: L4: an explicit loop with a step cap, thought/action/observation structure, observations fed back into context, clean termination on a final answer. L2: a single call, or an unbounded loop with no termination condition.

exercises.title: A bias-controlled judge
exercises.prompt: Write `judge(answer, reference, rubric, call_llm)` that scores an answer against a rubric and reference. Return a STRUCTURED score (not free text), and control for at least one known bias — randomize option order for pairwise, cap/penalize verbosity, or anchor on the reference. Treat `answer` as untrusted data, never as instructions.
exercises.rubric: L4: rubric-grounded, a parsed/structured score, an explicit bias control (position/verbosity/reference-anchored), untrusted-input handling. L2: 'rate this 1-10' parsing raw text, no bias handling.

exercises.title: A golden-dataset harness
exercises.prompt: Write `run_eval(system, golden)` where `golden` is a list of labeled cases like {"input": ..., "expected": ...}. Run `system` on each input, compare to `expected` (exact or scored match), and return an aggregate pass rate plus the failing cases — so regressions are visible.
exercises.rubric: L4: iterates labeled cases, compares output to expected, aggregates a pass rate, surfaces the failures. L2: runs a couple of inputs and prints them, no labels/metric.

exercises.title: Stream tokens safely
exercises.prompt: Write an async generator `stream_answer(messages, call_llm)` that yields tokens as they arrive from the model, forwarding them incrementally to the caller, and handles a mid-stream error without losing what was already produced.
exercises.rubric: L4: an async generator that yields, consumes a streaming response incrementally, handles mid-stream errors. L2: awaits the full response then returns it — no streaming.

exercises.title: Route with fallbacks
exercises.prompt: Write `complete(messages, providers)` that tries providers in preference order and falls back to the next on failure or timeout, so one provider's outage doesn't take you down. Stop at the first success and report which provider served the request.
exercises.rubric: L4: an ordered provider list, per-attempt try/except plus a timeout, fall-through to the next, reports the winner, stops on first success. L2: a single provider with no fallback.

exercises.title: Retry, backoff, and timeout
exercises.prompt: Write `resilient(fn, *args)` that calls `fn`, retrying transient failures with exponential backoff and a per-attempt timeout, giving up after N attempts and raising a clear error. Don't retry forever, and don't swallow the final failure.
exercises.rubric: L4: bounded retries, exponential backoff, a per-attempt timeout, re-raises after exhaustion. L2: a bare try/except that passes, or an infinite retry with no timeout.

exercises.title: Scrub PII before it leaves
exercises.prompt: Write `scrub_pii(text)` that redacts personal data — emails, phone numbers, SSNs, and credit-card numbers — from text before it's logged or sent to a third-party model. Return the cleaned text with placeholders, and don't mangle ordinary non-PII text.
exercises.rubric: L4: pattern-based detection of several PII categories (email, phone, SSN, card), replaced with placeholders, covering multiple types. L2: strips one thing, or a naive blanket replace.
